item.title: Reaping What She Sows: Women at the Forefront of Toronto Food Systems Change - by Toronto Public Library — Sat Oct 10, 3:00 PM — Toronto Public Library - Lillian H. Smith Branch
item.description:
More info: https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/events/6a95d6d21c197d11325c2d52
Hosted by Toronto Public Library (https://www.torontopubliclibrary.ca)
Global events - from pandemics, war, and foodborne illnesses - have threatened farmers' livelihoods, created supermarket shortages, and revealed to consumers that our food system is broken. Nancy Matsumoto will introduce her book and highlight Toronto women changemakers building up local and regional supply chains to combat the destructive effects of Big Food.
Source: Show Up Toronto

item.title: Mold-Making 101 with Janet Macpherson | 2 Weekends — Sat Oct 17, 10:00 AM — 300 Campbell Avenue
item.description: Dates : Saturday and Sunday October 17-18 & 24-25 2026 Times : 10:00am - 4:00pm Location : 300 Campbell Avenue, Unit 115 Instructor : Janet Macpherson Unlock new creative possibilities in ceramics with our comprehensive Mold-Making 101 course. This hands-on class will guide you through the process of designing and creating plaster molds for both slip casting and press molding techniques. You’ll learn how to craft one-part and two-part molds, make decorative sprig molds, and combine slip-cast pieces into finished ceramic forms. This course is best for those with some hand-building experience. Throughout the course, you'll explore: - The fundamentals of plaster and its use in mold-making. - Techniques for creating and using press molds and sprig molds. - How to design and construct two-part molds for more complex shapes. - The basics of slip casting and assembling multi-part pieces. - Finishing techniques to prepare your work for firing and glazing. item.title: 🍂 Fall Walk of Toronto Island 🌊🌆! 9KM — Sat Oct 17, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years! # 🍂🌊 FALL WALK: TORONTO ISLANDS 🌊🍁
### Island Paths, Fall Colours & Toronto's Best Urban Escape
There is something magical about the Toronto Islands in the fall. Once the summer crowds disappear, the islands become quieter and more peaceful. The changing leaves, crisp air, open green spaces, quiet cottages, and golden light over the water make it one of the best times of year to explore. And then there's the skyline.
From the islands, you get some of the best views of Toronto anywhere in the city — especially when the fall colours frame the downtown skyline across the water.
Join us for a relaxed fall walk through **Hanlan's Point, Centre Island, and Ward's Island**, enjoying the scenery, fresh air, and great conversation along the way. This is approximately **9 km**, with mostly flat paths and no major hills. It's a longer walk, but the pace will be relaxed and we'll take breaks along the way
